status: fixed in this follow-up branch; no live Reach deployment
scope: Follow-up to PR 53, using the merged public repository as the baseline.

findings.symptom: A shared CLI connection process dies after dispatching a POST but before returning its answer; the caller takes over and dispatches the POST again.
findings.evidence: The uninstrumented production main -> open path dispatched an inert synthetic job twice. The fixed path dispatches it once and reports an uncertain outcome with instructions to check the result.
findings.fix: Retry unsent writes only when the local connection explicitly proves notRun. Reads may recover automatically. A lost write answer never inherits that guarantee.
tests: the production CLI never replays a POST whose holder died after dispatch

findings.symptom: A request rejected for device identity, signing key, connection type, connector address or OAuth client can still activate a pending credential or end the legitimate connection through reuse detection.
findings.evidence: Independent synthetic device, browser and hosted refresh tests show legitimate access disappearing after rejected requests on public main.
findings.fix: Validate the credential's binding before settling rotation, recording use or notifying reuse; recheck the binding under the credential-store lock.
findings.limit: The demonstrated impact is unauthorized state mutation and loss of legitimate access. These tests do not demonstrate a read or control permission bypass.
tests: a rejected device identity cannot activate or revoke another device's rotated credential
a wrong signing key or connection type cannot settle another agent's credential rotation
a retired device credential presented by a different node cannot end the active session
a retired browser credential presented with another key cannot end the active session
a retired hosted refresh token at another connector cannot end the active session
a refresh at the wrong connector or with the wrong OAuth client cannot alter rotated access

findings.symptom: An old pending credential remains usable after Reopen link or session renewal; old retired credentials can also terminate the replacement session.
findings.evidence: On public main, a pending credential from the previous browser session is accepted after Reopen link and after reconnecting.
findings.fix: Clear pending and retired credential hashes atomically when replacing, reopening or starting a browser admission.
tests: renewing a browser session retires every credential from the previous session
renewing a browser session retires every credential from the previous session after Reopen link

findings.symptom: Concurrent CLI calls rotate twice, and competing public-link renewals invalidate each other's receipts. Delayed refusals can replace an already renewed session.
findings.evidence: Real separate CLI processes and persisted synthetic admissions reproduce duplicate rotations and failed concurrent calls. A delayed rejection also triggers a second unnecessary renewal.
findings.fix: Share one holder per canonical connection folder, one socket connection and one renewal promise. Reload saved credentials before takeover; adopt a successor already saved by another call.
tests: concurrent production CLI calls share a single credential rotation
concurrent refused agent calls share one reconnect and all resume their valid Always grant
a late rejection adopts the token another call already renewed
after rejection an agent reloads a credential another process saved before reconnecting

findings.symptom: Two requests fail on the private route concurrently; one consumes the other's shared fallback cursor, so a request fails without trying the working public route.
findings.fix: Keep a fallback cursor per request while retaining the shared preferred endpoint for later requests.
tests: concurrent private route failures each reach the public fallback

findings.symptom: A failed socket emits a delayed close event after its replacement connects; the old event rejects the replacement's in-flight request.
findings.fix: Only the currently selected socket may clear requests or deliver answers. Old connection acquisitions cannot erase a newer selection.
tests: a failed shared socket's delayed close cannot reject a newer connection's request

findings.symptom: Two tabs using the same Always access renew independently, or a second tab rejects an action while the first tab replaces the session.
findings.fix: Use an optional Web Lock around renewal and saved-session reads, then adopt the session already saved by the other tab.
tests: two tabs with Always access share one renewal and adopt its saved token
a second tab waits for an in-flight renewal before dispatching its action
without Web Locks, simultaneous requests in one tab share their renewal
findings.limit: Cross-tab tests use a deterministic LockManager mock. Without Web Locks, the existing same-tab promise coordination remains the fallback. Actual mobile browsers were not exercised.

findings.symptom: Browser renewal errors and lost answers from resent actions are swallowed into the original 401/Not-Run response; CLI renewal errors similarly lose their actual status or collection reason.
findings.evidence: HTTP 503, network drop, timeout and explicit refusal fixtures reproduce stale statuses. A resent synthetic browser write dispatches once but its lost answer is incorrectly marked Not-Run on public main.
findings.fix: Preserve renewal errors and refusal statuses. Catch renewal failures separately from a resent action's uncertain outcome. Never mark a lost action answer safe to repeat.
tests: a temporary renewal HTTP 503 remains retryable and never repeats a browser action
a temporary renewal network drop remains retryable and never repeats a browser action
a temporary renewal network timeout remains retryable and never repeats a browser action
a lost action answer after successful renewal is never marked safe to repeat
reconnect reports its actual refusal instead of the original generic session error
a refused credential collection retains its actual reason

findings.symptom: A renewal receipt is saved, but collection fails or its one-time answer is lost. Later requests have no session and cannot reach the normal reconnect path.
findings.fix: Resume credential collection from the saved approved receipt under the renewal lock; use the existing reconnect fallback when that credential was already collected.
tests: credential collection recovers after a temporary outage without replaying an action
credential collection recovers after a lost one-time credential answer without replaying an action

findings.symptom: An in-flight browser request authenticates with its retired credential during the documented two-minute grace, but lease renewal rejects the same credential as ended.
findings.fix: Use the same current-or-live-retired credential rule when touching the browser lease.
tests: a retired browser credential can renew its lease during the in-flight grace period

findings.symptom: A stale service catalog requests access that the owner already approved; the UI briefly shows waiting for approval until its next three-second poll.
findings.fix: Execute an already approved response immediately. Wait only for a pending response, and display ended or refused responses accurately.
tests: a stale catalog uses an already approved service request immediately
findings.limit: This is a temporary false wait, not a permanent hang. Service permissions and consent policy are unchanged.
